saliency_check.method: Deletion test on the dual-stream member

summary: The detector rates this image likely real (score <0.1%). 0 of 3 ensemble members lean AI. This is a likelihood assessment, not proof; the cues below list the measured signals behind it.
localization_quality: SmoothGrad pixel sensitivity of the dual-stream member, the member that drives the stacked decision, computed at its native input resolution. Shows which pixels the score is most sensitive to; the deletion check cue tests whether they matter. Not a verified localization of generation artifacts.

cues.detail: dima806/deepfake_vs_real_image_detection (ViT-Base/16 (in21k), fine-tuned) scores P(AI) 35.8%. Its share of the stacked log-odds is -0.20 (toward real).
Organika/sdxl-detector (Swin, fine-tuned on Wikimedia vs SDXL pairs) scores P(AI) <0.1%. Its share of the stacked log-odds is -0.23 (toward real).
SignalScope PyTorch Dual-Stream Backbone (ResNet34 + 2D Fast Fourier Transform (FFT)) scores P(AI) <0.1%. Its share of the stacked log-odds is -8.71 (toward real).

Replacing the 10% most salient pixels changes the dual-stream log-odds by +0.62; the same number of random pixels changes it by +1.36 (mean of 5 draws). Here salient pixels do not move the score more than random ones, so treat the map with caution.
Share of spectral power above half-Nyquist on a native-resolution crop. Reported for inspection only; it is not calibrated as a detector and does not drive the verdict.
